subtitleNullable: PubChem documentation and candidate fingerprints for molecular identification
descriptionNullable:
When several candidate structures fit a mass spectrum equally well, the one better documented in PubChem is often the right answer, especially for natural products: among all PubChem structures of the same mass, the right answer of a panel natural product is the best-documented one in 66% of cases. This dataset gives PubChem documentation and source annotations (substance records, PubMed articles, patents, MeSH terms, synonyms, depositors, natural-product membership and LOTUS literature counts) for the 106 million structures of a mass-sorted PubChem tier and the 711,000 structures of the public candidate pool, aligned row by row so that a notebook can use them offline. It also holds a structural fingerprint for every tier structure, so a notebook can score PubChem candidates without computing fingerprints at run time. The [data notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/dmitriigluzdov/casmi-26-the-data-behind-spectra-to-structures) adds 0.15 × a documentation score, ln(1 + substances) + ln(1 + PubMed articles) plus small bonuses for spectral-library depositors, natural-product membership, LOTUS references and synonyms, to its PubChem search.

![Caffeine and isocaffeine have the same formula but different PubChem documentation counts.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gluzdov-Dmitrii/Enveda-CASMI-2026/main/kaggle-datasets/casmi26-pubchem-popularity-prior/same_formula_documentation.png)

## Features

| Group | Feature | Files | What it tells |
|---|---|---|---|
| Documentation | Substance records | `*_lsid` | How many PubChem substance records point to the structure, as ln(1 + n). |
| | PubMed articles | `*_lpmid` | Linked PubMed articles, as ln(1 + n). |
| | Patents | `*_lpatent` | Linked patents, as ln(1 + n). |
| | MeSH terms | `*_lmesh` | Distinct medical subject headings of the representative compound, as ln(1 + n). |
| | Synonyms | `*_lsynonyms` | Names recorded for the representative compound, as ln(1 + n). |
| Who deposited it | Depositors and vendors | `*_n_depositors`, `*_n_vendors` | Distinct depositors of the representative compound, and how many of them are chemical vendors. |
| | Depositor groups | `*_src_mask` | Bits: 1 spectral library, 2 metabolite or pathway database, 4 natural-product database, 8 ChEBI, 16 LIPID MAPS, 32 drug database, 128 toxicology, 256 chemical vendor, 512 Wikidata. |
| Natural products | Membership | `*_np` | Bits: 1 COCONUT, 2 LOTUS, 4 NPAtlas. |
| | LOTUS references | `*_lotus_refs` | Literature references recorded for the structure in LOTUS. |
| Chemistry | Formula isomers | `*_formula_isomers` | How many tier structures share the formula, that is, how crowded the candidate list of that formula is. |
| | Parent compound | `pool_parent_cid`, `pool_has_different_parent`, `pc_different_parent_rows` | Whether the representative compound belongs to a different PubChem parent compound, for example as a salt. |
| | Fingerprint | `fingerprints-*.bin` | 10,226-bit structural fingerprint of every tier structure (see below). |
| Identity | Compound and key | `*_cid`, `pc_ik14` | The representative PubChem compound and its InChIKey connectivity block. |

`pc_*` files follow the rows of the PubChem tier, `pool_*` files the rows of the candidate pool, and `delta_pc_*` and `growth_pc_*` the rows of the two supplements below.

| Structures covered | Files | Rows |
|---|---|---:|
| PubChem tier, sorted by neutral mass | `casmi26-pubchem-tier/pc_mass.npy`, `pc_off.npy`, `pc_smiles.npy` and `pc_*` | 105,875,489 |
| Supplement added in version 4, absent from the tier | `delta_pc_*`, `delta_pubchem_tier.csv` | 36,303 |
| Supplement of 2026-10-20: qualifying structures absent from the tier and the earlier supplement (PubChem release of 2026-10-19) | `growth_pc_*`, `growth_pubchem_tier.csv` | 11,177 |
| Public candidate pool (training structures and COCONUT), with names | `pool_*`, `pool_popularity.csv` | 710,701 |
| PubChemLite candidates of the second engine | `pubchemlite_annotations.parquet` | 385,760 |

Depositor groups were not measured for the supplements; `*_src_observed` marks the rows where they were.

## Who is the best-documented candidate

![Among PubChem structures within 10 ppm of the right answer, the answer is the best documented for 66% of panel natural products, 24% of training natural products and 2% of other training molecules; the median answer beats 99.8%, 99.0% and 66.0% of its candidates.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gluzdov-Dmitrii/Enveda-CASMI-2026/main/kaggle-datasets/casmi26-pubchem-popularity-prior/answer_rank_by_documentation.png)

For each molecule, the figure ranks all PubChem tier structures within 10 ppm of the right answer's neutral mass by ln(1 + substances) + ln(1 + PubMed articles). The right answer of a panel natural product is the best-documented structure of its mass in 66% of cases, and the median answer is better documented than 99.8% of its candidates. Natural products in a random sample of 10,000 training molecules behave alike (24% and 99.0%). The other training molecules are rarely the best documented (2%), although still above most of their candidates (66.0%). A documentation prior therefore helps most with natural products, which is what the hidden test's molecules from biological extracts are, and a large weight can push down a correct but rarely studied structure. In our test, a prior learned from training molecules did worse on the panel than the hand-made one (MRR@25 0.886 against 0.970).

## How to use it

- **Add the prior.** Add `w × (pc_lsid + pc_lpmid)` to a standardised spectral score of each candidate; the data notebook uses w = 0.15 and adds the bonuses listed above before the weight.
- **Search PubChem by mass.** `casmi26-pubchem-tier/pc_mass.npy` is sorted, so `np.searchsorted` gives the rows of a 10 ppm window; search the two supplements the same way, or use `CandidateView` below for all three at once.
- **Score candidates by fingerprint.** Compare a fingerprint predicted from the spectrum with the stored fingerprints of the window instead of running RDKit on every candidate.
- **Build your own features.** Every column of the Features table is aligned with the tier and the pool, so a ranker can combine them; check a learned prior on natural products, not only on training molecules.

## Quick start

The example reads the dataset from either supported Kaggle mount location.

```python
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
slug = 'casmi26-pubchem-popularity-prior'
D = next(p for p in (Path('/kaggle/input/datasets/dmitriigluzdov') / slug, Path('/kaggle/input') / slug) if p.is_dir())
pool = pd.read_csv(D / 'pool_popularity.csv')
print(pool.loc[pool.inchikey14.isin(['RYYVLZVUVIJVGH', 'LPHGQDQBBGAPDZ']), ['compound_name', 'pop', 'n_depositors']])
```

## Candidate fingerprints

Every tier structure has a 10,226-bit fingerprint computed with [RDKit](https://www.rdkit.org/). Each bit is the answer to one yes/no question about the structure (1 = yes, 0 = no). Some questions concern the whole molecule (MACCS keys, such as "is there a C=O double bond?"), others are asked for every atom with its neighbours (Morgan) and for every pair of atoms with the number of bonds between them (atom pairs), and the rest for chains of bonds (paths and torsions). Seven families of such questions are joined into one vector. The picture shows a few of them for caffeine.

![A fingerprint bit is the answer to a yes/no question about the structure: for caffeine, C=O double bond 1, aromatic ring 1, halogen 0, this N with exactly these neighbours 1, C=O oxygen two bonds from an N 1.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gluzdov-Dmitrii/Enveda-CASMI-2026/main/kaggle-datasets/casmi26-pubchem-popularity-prior/fingerprint_from_rdkit.png)

The seven families are Morgan radius 2 and 3, feature Morgan radius 2, paths up to six bonds, atom pairs, topological torsions and MACCS keys. The fingerprints are stored in twelve files `fingerprints-000.bin` … `fingerprints-011.bin` (69 GB). The bit selection is the one of the public candidate pool (`fp_bits.npy`), so tier and pool fingerprints can be compared directly, and a model trained to predict pool fingerprints from spectra can score tier candidates as they are. A check of 606 rows from all parts against fresh RDKit 2026.03.3 fingerprints found no difference.

`fingerprint_index.py` needs only NumPy and reads just the requested rows. `CandidateView` searches a mass window in the tier and both supplements at once and returns the rows sorted by mass, with their origin and row number.

```python
from fingerprint_index import CandidateView, FingerprintIndex

view = CandidateView(D)
hits = view.window(300.1234, ppm=10,
                   fields=('lsid', 'lpmid', 'lsynonyms', 'src_observed'),
                   smiles=True)
# origin: 0 = tier, 1 = delta, 2 = growth; source_row counts within that origin.
index = FingerprintIndex(D, collection='pubchem')
tier = hits['origin'] == 0
packed, formulas, status = index.get(hits['source_row'][tier], view='public')
```

Fingerprints are stored for the tier only; for the 47,480 supplement structures, compute them with the same featurizer. Structures that RDKit cannot parse have status 1 and an empty fingerprint. `INDEX.json` describes the file layout.

## Overlap with the competition data

Of 275,810 distinct training-file connectivity keys (the first 14 InChIKey characters), 256,476 occur in the PubChem tier and 271,463 in the pool.

## Other files

| Files | Contents |
|---|---|
| `pool_popularity.csv`, `pubchem_tier_sample.csv`, `delta_pubchem_tier.csv`, `growth_pubchem_tier.csv` | Readable CSV views with names, counts and keys. |
| `SOURCE_GROUPS.csv`, `SOURCE_INVENTORY.csv`, `SOURCE_CATALOGUE.csv`, `SOURCE_GROUP_STATUS.csv` | Which PubChem depositors belong to each depositor group. |
| `BENCHMARK_*.csv`, `BENCHMARK_*_METHOD.json`, `formula_failures.parquet`, `FORMULA_*.json` | Documentation-only ranking comparisons on the panel and the formula-count method. |
| `PUBCHEM_EXTRAS.json`, `GROWTH_*.json`, `LOTUS_REFRESH.json`, `MANIFEST*.json`, `INDEX.json`, `FILE_DESCRIPTIONS.json` | Source files, retrieval dates, checksums, the fingerprint layout and a description of every file. |
| `ATTRIBUTION.md`, `VALIDATION*.json`, `REPORT.json`, `*COVERAGE*.json`, `JOIN_NOTES.json`, `pool_match.json`, `tier_match.json`, `delta_meta.json` | Credits, source checks, validation results and join records. |
| `aligned_public_priors.py`, `fingerprint_index.py` | Helpers to align the priors and to read fingerprints. |
| `scripts/` | Build and check scripts with their dated manifests and checks. |
| `TECHNICAL_NOTES.md` | Column definitions, build steps and validation. |

## How it was made

Public PubChem files were matched to the tier and the pool, and one representative PubChem compound was chosen for each match. Substance, PubMed and patent counts combine matching stereoisomers [forms with the same atom connections but a different spatial arrangement]; depositor, vendor, MeSH and synonym counts describe the representative compound. Natural-product membership and LOTUS counts come from the [natural-product knowledge table](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/dmitriigluzdov/casmi26-natural-product-knowledge-table), built on LOTUS 2026-04-13 and NPAtlas v2024_09. Fingerprints were computed with RDKit from the tier SMILES. Independent joins, file hashes and count checks are included.

## Updates

- **2026-10-27:** Added fingerprints of all 105.9 million tier structures and a loader that searches the tier and both supplements by mass. Build scripts and dated check files moved to `scripts/`; all data files keep their names and contents.
- **2026-10-20, second update:** Natural-product bits and LOTUS counts rebuilt on LOTUS 2026-04-13 (17,722 tier and 6,458 pool membership values, 81,956 and 12,041 reference counts); corrected the LOTUS licence and the description of the 11,177 added structures; a complete file index.
- **2026-10-20:** Added 11,177 qualifying PubChem structures absent from the tier and the earlier supplement (PubChem release of 2026-10-19) and the missing synonym, natural-product and LOTUS arrays of the earlier supplement; the data notebook's PubChem search now covers the tier and both supplements.
- **2026-10-19, second update:** Added synonym, parent and formula annotations; synonyms gave a small gain of about 0.004 MRR@25 [mean reciprocal answer rank within the first 25 guesses, zero outside that list] at fixed weights 0.25 and 0.50 on exact-formula panel candidates.
- **2026-10-19:** Added aligned LOTUS reference counts, PubChemLite documentation and alignment helpers.

## Licence and credits

**Courtesy of the U.S. National Library of Medicine.** This dated PubChem snapshot is not the latest release, and NLM does not endorse the dataset. PubChem-generated information is public-domain U.S. government information; contributed material can carry source-specific rights. Reuse follows the [NCBI data-use policy](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/about/policies/), [NLM FTP terms](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/databases/download/terms_and_conditions.html) and [PubChem source guidance](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/docs/downloads). Cite [Kim et al., PubChem 2025 update](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkae1059).

LOTUS counts and membership use the frozen release of 2026-04-13 ([Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19360665)), CC BY 4.0; credit [Rutz et al.](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.70780). NPAtlas data are [CC BY-NC 4.0](https://www.npatlas.org/download): non-commercial use with attribution to [van Santen et al. and contributors](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkab941). The mass-sorted PubChem tier is [Ahmed Berat Özer’s](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ahmedberatozer/casmi26-pubchem-tier); COCONUT membership and the fingerprint bit selection follow his [public pool](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ahmedberatozer/casmi26-v2-pool).

The popularity formulation appeared in [wangpenghua’s notebook](https://www.kaggle.com/code/wangpenghua/casmi26-v21-v4i-pop); these counts were independently rebuilt from primary PubChem files. Related methods are [MetFrag](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9) and [PubChemLite](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-021-00489-0). The dataset contains no competition spectra or answer tables.

Related methods are [MetFrag](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-016-0115-9) and [PubChemLite](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13321-021-00489-0). The dataset contains no competition spectra or answer tables.
